bear.food: Berries, roots, salmon, sometimes elk calves
bear.name: Brown bear
bear.role: Carries salmon from rivers into the forest, feeding the trees.
bear.social: Mostly alone. Mothers keep their cubs for two to three years.
bear.where: Forests and mountains of North America, Europe and Asia

beaver.name: Beaver
beaver.role: Builds dams that make ponds, a home for fish, frogs and birds.
beaver.social: Families of a mother, a father and their young share one lodge.
beaver.where: Rivers and lakes of North America and Europe

bee.life: Workers about 6 weeks, the queen 2–5 years
bee.name: Honeybee
bee.role: Pollinates about a third of the food people eat.
bee.social: Colonies of 20,000–60,000: one queen and many workers whose job changes with age.
bee.where: Worldwide, wild and kept by beekeepers

cheetah.name: Cheetah
cheetah.role: The fastest runner on land: up to 110 km/h, but only for a short sprint.
cheetah.social: Mothers raise cubs alone; brothers often stay together for life.
cheetah.where: Open grasslands of Africa, a few in Iran

elephant.food: Grass, bark and fruit: about 150 kg a day
elephant.name: African elephant
elephant.role: Opens up woodland, digs water holes and spreads seeds.
elephant.social: Herds of related females led by the oldest, the matriarch. Males leave at about 13.

elk.name: Elk
elk.role: The main meal of wolves; their grazing shapes the forest edge.
elk.social: Mothers and young live in big herds; males live alone and roar (bugle) in autumn.
elk.where: Mountain forests and meadows of North America and Asia

fox.name: Red fox
fox.role: Keeps rabbit and mouse numbers in check.
fox.social: Pairs raise their cubs together; older daughters sometimes help.
fox.where: Almost everywhere in the northern half of the world, even in cities

gazelle.name: Gazelle
gazelle.role: Food for cheetahs, lions and hyenas; can run a zig-zag at 80 km/h.
gazelle.social: Herds of females and young; males guard small patches of land.

hornet.food: Bees and other insects (for its young), fruit and nectar
hornet.life: Workers a few weeks, queens about a year
hornet.name: Hornet
hornet.role: Hovers outside beehives and catches bees as they fly home.
hornet.social: Paper nests of a few thousand, started each spring by one queen.

jackal.name: Black-backed jackal
jackal.role: Hunts small animals and cleans up what others leave.
jackal.social: Pairs for life; last year's pups help raise the new litter.
jackal.where: Dry grassland and desert edges of southern and eastern Africa

lion.name: Lion
lion.role: Keeps grazing herds healthy and on the move.
lion.social: Prides of related females with 1–3 males. The females hunt together.
lion.where: Savannas of Africa, and one forest in India

lseal.name: Leopard seal
lseal.role: Top hunter on the sea ice, after the orca.

meerkat.name: Meerkat
meerkat.role: Eats huge numbers of insects; food for jackals and eagles.
meerkat.social: Mobs of 20–50 led by one breeding pair; others babysit and take turns as lookouts.
meerkat.where: Kalahari and Namib deserts, southern Africa

orca.food: Fish or seals, depending on the pod
orca.name: Orca
orca.role: Top hunter of the sea, shaping seal and fish numbers.
orca.social: Pods led by grandmothers. Each pod has its own calls and hunting tricks.
orca.where: Every ocean, most common in cold water

penguin.name: Emperor penguin
penguin.role: Tells scientists how healthy the sea ice is.
penguin.social: Colonies of thousands. Fathers huddle together and keep the egg warm all winter.

rabbit.name: Rabbit
rabbit.role: Food for foxes, hawks and many others; can strip land bare when there are too many.
rabbit.social: Live in groups in underground tunnels called warrens.
rabbit.where: Grassland and woodland edges; spread by people to many countries

salmon.name: Atlantic salmon
salmon.role: Carries ocean food far inland; food for bears, seals and birds.
salmon.social: Alone at sea; adults swim back to the river they hatched in to lay eggs.
salmon.where: The North Atlantic and the rivers that flow into it

scorpion.name: Scorpion
scorpion.role: Hunts insects at night; meerkats are immune to many of their stings.
scorpion.social: Alone. Mothers carry their babies on their back.
scorpion.where: Deserts and dry lands on every continent except Antarctica

seal.name: Harbour seal
seal.role: Eats fish; food for orcas and sharks.
seal.social: Rest together on beaches and rocks, but hunt alone.
seal.where: Cold coasts of the North Atlantic and North Pacific

wolf.name: Gray wolf
wolf.role: Keeps elk on the move, which lets riverside trees grow back.
wolf.social: Packs of 4–9: a mother, a father and their young. The "alpha" pair are simply the parents.
wolf.where: Forests, tundra and mountains across North America, Europe and Asia

zebra.name: Zebra
zebra.role: Eats the tall grass first, opening the way for gazelles.
zebra.social: Families of one stallion, several mares and foals; families join into big herds.
zebra.where: Grasslands of eastern and southern Africa
